name: Shillong
description: Shillong is the capital of Meghalaya, a hill station at roughly 1,500 m elevation known for its rolling pine-covered hills, heavy monsoon rains, and a distinct Anglo-Khasi cultural character. It suits travelers who enjoy cool weather, living root bridges, and a slower pace; serious adventure seekers or beach lovers will find it less compelling.
nearest_railhead: Guwahati Railway Station (approx. 100 km from Shillong)
nearest_airport: Shillong Airport (Umroi), 35 km; Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati, 128 km (more flights)

attractions.name: Ward's Lake
attractions.description: A colonial-era artificial lake in the heart of Shillong with a bridge, rowboats, and manicured gardens. Pleasant for a casual stroll but small enough that an hour covers it comfortably.

attractions.name: Elephant Falls
attractions.description: A three-tiered waterfall about 12 km from the city centre, easily accessible by road. The lower tiers are scenic but the site can get crowded on weekends; the steps to the lower level are steep and uneven.

attractions.name: Shillong Peak
attractions.description: The highest point near Shillong at about 1,965 m, offering a panoramic view of the city and surrounding hills. Access requires an Indian Air Force permit; the final stretch is a short walk on a paved path.

attractions.name: Umiam Lake (Barapani)
attractions.description: A large reservoir about 15 km north of Shillong ringed by pine and deciduous forest. Water sports are available at the MTDC complex; the drive itself along NH6 is scenic, especially at dusk.

attractions.name: Mawlynnong Village
attractions.description: Often called Asia's cleanest village, Mawlynnong is about 90 km from Shillong near the Bangladesh border. The single-tier living root bridge and sky-walk are the highlights; it is best visited on a full-day trip combined with Dawki.

attractions.name: Dawki and Umngot River
attractions.description: The Umngot river at Dawki has some of the clearest water in India; boats appear to float on glass in the dry season (November to April). The border town is rough around the edges but the river experience is genuinely striking.

attractions.name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge, Nongriat
attractions.description: A famous double-decker bridge grown from the aerial roots of rubber fig trees, reached by descending roughly 3,500 steps from Tyrna village near Cherrapunji. The trek takes 3-4 hours round trip and is not suitable for those with knee problems or poor fitness.

attractions.name: Nohkalikai Falls, Cherrapunji
attractions.description: One of the tallest plunge waterfalls in India at about 340 m, located near Cherrapunji (Sohra) roughly 55 km from Shillong. The viewpoint is accessible with a short walk from the parking area; the falls are most dramatic during and just after the monsoon.

attractions.name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
attractions.description: A seven-floor museum in Laitumkhrah documenting the indigenous cultures of Northeast India with artifacts, costumes, and a rooftop sky-walk offering city views. One of the most professionally curated ethnographic museums in the region.

attractions.name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
attractions.description: A 78-hectare ancient sacred grove about 25 km from Shillong, preserved by Khasi tradition and off-limits to any extraction. Guided walks reveal dense old-growth forest, medicinal plants, and monoliths; it is a genuine hidden gem compared to the better-known tourist sites.

attractions.name: Laitlum Canyons
attractions.description: A lesser-visited canyon viewpoint about 30 km from Shillong near Smit village, offering sweeping views of deep gorges and terraced hills with very few crowds. The site involves a moderate walk on an uneven path to reach the best vantage points.
